title: Gabber global projective alteration with a relative strict normal crossings boundary
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\ell$ be a prime different from $\operatorname{char}(k)$, let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $Z\subseteq X$ be a nowhere dense closed subset. There exist a finite field extension $k'/k$ of degree prime to $\ell$ [def-pc-field-extension], a smooth quasi-projective $k'$-scheme $P$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and a proper projective surjective morphism $a:P\to X$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] compatible with $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, such that $a$ sends every generic point of an irreducible component of $P$ to a generic point of an irreducible component of $X$, and induces there finite residue-field extensions of degree prime to $\ell$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-residue-field]. The reduced inverse image of $Z$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor on $P/k'$: it has finitely many distinct irreducible components $D_i$, each smooth over $k'$ and of codimension one, with every intersection $\bigcap_{i\in J}D_i$ smooth over $k'$ and of codimension $|J|$ wherever nonempty. Locally at a point of $P$, the components through that point have equations given by distinct members of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. In particular this reduced inverse image is a strict normal crossings boundary in the regular-scheme sense [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Here quasi-projective means admitting a locally closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over $k'$. Empty schemes, empty boundaries and empty intersections are allowed.

source.place: Expose X, Theorem 2.1 and definition of an ell-prime alteration immediately before it; printed pp. 148--149. Relative strict normal crossings is explained immediately after the theorem; VIII 4.1.2 and Remark 4.2.2(i).

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, take $k'=k$ and $P=\varnothing$; all conditions are vacuous. Otherwise apply proper-pair radicial preparation to obtain $X\subseteq\overline X$, $C$, $e/k$ and $r:B\to\overline X$, with $C\cap X=Z$.

Apply the equivariant smooth Galois-model lemma to $(B,r^{-1}C)/e$. Its hypotheses hold by preparation, including geometric reducedness and the effective Cartier boundary. Obtain one common $K,G,Y,h$, with radicial $K^G/e$, the full-quotient universal-homeomorphism property, all subgroup quotients, and relative SNC divisor $D=(h^{-1}r^{-1}C)_{\rm red}$.

Apply semilinear Sylow SNC resolution to this model, with boundary $r^{-1}C$. This gives $F=K^L$, $Q^\circ$, $d$, $R$, $v$ and $E$. In particular $[F:e]$ and every generic residue degree for $d$ are prime to $\ell$, $v$ preserves generic residue fields, and $|E|=(d v)^{-1}r^{-1}C$. Set $c=r d v$.

The composite $c$ is surjective and sends all component generic points to generic points. In positive characteristic $p$, the purely inseparable extensions $e/k$ and the generic residue extensions of $r$ have towers with successive degrees $p$; multiplying field bases gives degrees $p^n$. In characteristic zero they are trivial. Thus they are prime to $\ell$. Multiplying bases in each residue-field tower gives degree $1\cdot\deg(d)\cdot\deg(r)$ prime to $\ell$ for every generic point of $R$, and $[F:k]=[F:e][e:k]$ is prime to $\ell$.

source.place: X 2.3 Steps 1--3, composition of the alterations.

proof.text: Apply finite-constant projective-graph projectivity to $F/k$, $R$ and $c:R\to\overline X$: $R$ is projective over $F$ and $\overline X$ is separated over $k$. Set $k'=F$ and $P=c^{-1}X$. Its base-change clause gives that $a:P\to X$ is proper and projective in both conventions. Surjective base change makes $a$ surjective.

source.place: X 2.3, return to the original open and final composite, pp.150,152.

proof.text: Apply open smooth SNC restriction to $(R,E)$ and $P\subseteq R$. It supplies smoothness, quasi-projectivity and every relative, local-parameter and regular-boundary assertion. Since $C\cap X=Z$, $|E|\cap P=a^{-1}Z$, so its reduced boundary is the required one. Every generic point of $R$ lies in $P$: its image is generic in $\overline X$ and hence belongs to the dense open $X$. The generic residue degrees of $a$ are therefore precisely those already checked for $c$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_gabber_global_snc_alteration (k : Type u) [Field k] (ℓ : ℕ) (hℓ : Nat.Prime ℓ) (hchar : ℓ ≠ ringChar k) (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (Z : Set X) (hZ : IsClosed Z) (hZnd : interior Z = ∅) : ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (i : k →+* K), i.Finite ∧ Nat.Coprime (@Module.finrank k K _ _ i.toAlgebra.toModule) ℓ ∧ ∃ (P : Scheme.{u}) (p : P ⟶ Spec (.of K)) (a : P ⟶ X), Smooth p ∧ IsQuasiProjective p ∧ IsProper a ∧ IsProjectiveBundle a ∧ Surjective a ∧ a ≫ f = p ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i) ∧ (∀ (C : Set P), C ∈ irreducibleComponents P → ∀ η : P, IsGenericPoint η C → (∃ B ∈ irreducibleComponents X, IsGenericPoint (a η) B) ∧ (a.residueFieldMap η).hom.Finite ∧ Nat.Coprime (@Module.finrank (X.residueField (a η)) (P.residueField η) _ _ (a.residueFieldMap η).hom.toAlgebra.toModule) ℓ) ∧ ∃ D : P.IdealSheafData, D = ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal ⟨Z, hZ⟩).comap a).radical ∧ D.IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor p ∧ IsStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary D ∧ IsRegularScheme P ∧ ∀ x : P, ∃ (U : P.affineOpens) (hx : x ∈ U.1) (hR : IsNoetherianRing (P.presheaf.stalk x)) (t s : List (P.presheaf.stalk x)), @IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (P.presheaf.stalk x) _ _ hR t ∧ s.Sublist t ∧ s.Nodup ∧ (D.ideal U).map (P.presheaf.germ U.1 x hx).hom = Ideal.span {s.prod}
